head: dolça
etymology:
dol + -ça.
From Persian دولچه (dulče), diminutive of دول (dul).

head: dirçəliş
etymology: Morphologically, from dirçəl- (“to become animated”, verbal stem) + -iş. Compare diri (“alive”).

head: yataq
etymology: From yat- (“to sleep; to lie down”) + -aq. Cognate with Turkish yatak.
word_senses: bed (the bottom of a body of water)
abode, nest (a place where something or someones are to be found aplenty)
rookery (a colony of breeding sea animals)

head: deşik
etymology: From deşmək + -ik, from Proto-Turkic *deĺ- (“to make holes”). Doublet of dəlik. Cognate with Turkish deşik, Turkmen deşik.

head: yanacaq
base_senses: to burn, to get consumed by fire

head: islaq
etymology: Equivalent to islanmaq (“to become wet”) + -k. Compare Chuvash исленчӗк (islenč̬ĕk).

head: ibrətli
word_senses: didactic (instructive or intended to teach or demonstrate, especially with regard to morality)

head: dalaşmaq
etymology: From dala- (“bite”) + -ş. Cognate with Turkish dalaşmak. Compare to talischirmen (“I fight”) in the Codex Cumanicus.
word_senses: to scuffle, fight (to contend in physical conflict with each other)

head: şəfqət bacısı
etymology: Izafet II compound of şəfqət + bacı
expansion: Izafet II compound of şəfqət + bacı

head: karvansara
etymology: From earlier karvansaray, from Persian کاروانسرای (kârvânsarây). Equivalent to izafet I compound of karvan + saray.
expansion: izafet I compound of karvan + saray

head: cəzaçəkmə müəssisəsi
etymology: Izafet II compound of cəzaçəkmə (“serving the punishment”) + müəssisə (“facility”).
expansion: Izafet II compound of cəzaçəkmə (“serving the punishment”) + müəssisə (“facility”)

head: mina sahəsi
etymology: Izafet II compound of mina (“mine”) + sahə (“field”).
expansion: Izafet II compound of mina (“mine”) + sahə (“field”)

head: çatlamaq
etymology: From çat (“a crack”) + -la. Of onomatopoeic origin, see çırtlamaq. Cognate to Turkish çatlamak.

head: alçaltmaq
word_senses: to humiliate, to abase, to debase, degrade

head: çözələmək
word_senses: to unravel (to clear from complication or difficulty)
base_senses: to solve; to untie; to unravel

head: saraltı
base_senses: to turn yellow; to grow pale

head: tutuşdurmaq
base_senses: to catch fire; to burn; to flare up

head: bişmiş
base_senses: to be cooked, baked, roasted, become ready to eat

head: taleyüklü
word_senses: fateful (momentous, significant, setting or sealing one’s fate)

head: doğrultmaq
word_senses: to live up to (to fulfill the expectations placed upon)
to come true, to be fulfilled

head: dəzgah
etymology: From Persian دستگاه. Equivalent to dəst + -gah.

head: uydurma
base_senses: to make up, invent, imagine, or concoct

head: abadlaşdırmaq
etymology: Morphologically abadlaş- + -dır, from abad. Senses align with Russian благоустро́ить (blagoustróitʹ), suggesting semantic influence.
word_senses: to improve, to equip with modern amenities, (apartment) to face-lift, (city, park) to beautify, (street) to resurface
base_senses: to flourish, to prosper, to recover

head: düzülüş
word_senses: the act of arranging, putting together

head: qazanılmış immun çatışmazlığı sindromu
etymology: From qazanılmış (“acquired”) + immun çatışmazlığı (“immune deficiency”) + sindrom (“syndrome”). Calque from English.

head: çağırım
etymology: From çağır- + -ım. See cognates at Bashkir саҡрым (saqrım).

head: qurma
word_senses: set up, rigged, fixed, not real

head: mübadilə buferi
etymology: Calque of Russian бу́фер обме́на (búfer obména). Izafet II compound of mübadilə + bufer.
expansion: Izafet II compound of mübadilə + bufer
base_senses: Buffer: a memory area that temporarily holds data during transfer or processing.

head: əmanət kassası
etymology: Izafet II compound of əmanət + kassa. Calque of Russian сберега́тельная ка́сса (sberegátelʹnaja kássa).
expansion: Izafet II compound of əmanət + kassa

head: dölləndirmək
word_senses: to inseminate, to fertilize, to impregnate

head: çatlaşmaq
word_senses: to chat (to exchange text or voice messages)

head: birisigün
etymology:
From birisi + gün.
Cognates
Compare Karachay-Balkar бюрсюкюн (bürsükün) /бюрсикюн (bürsikün), Kumyk бирисигюн (birisigün), Kazakh бүрсігүні (bürsigüni), Nogai бирсигуьн (birsigün), Kyrgyz бүрсүгүнү (bürsügünü), Southern Altai бирсӱӱн (birsüün), Karaim birisikün etc., some of which mean 'the day before yesterday' and some - 'the day after tomorrow'.

head: agahlıq
word_senses: awareness (the state or quality of being aware of something)

head: girəcək
word_senses: vestibule (any of a number of body cavities or channels, serving as or resembling an entrance to another bodily space)

head: alım-satım
etymology: Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish آلم صاتم (alım satım). Antonymous compound of alım + satım. Literally, "buying and selling".

head: sıxışdırmaq
word_senses: to squeeze, to press tightly, to push to the side
to stick in, push in, insert forcefully

head: duyulmaz
base_senses: to be felt, to be noticed

head: həllolunmaz
etymology: From həll olunmaq (“to be solved, to dissolve”) + -maz.
expansion: həll olunmaq (“to be solved, to dissolve”) + -maz
word_senses: unsolvable (a problem that cannot be solved)

head: aralaşdırmaq
word_senses: to pull apart by force (people or animals that are fighting)

head: alqı-satqı
etymology:
Antonymous compound of alqı + satqı. Due to term being overrepresented, it is difficult to pinpoint the original source. For a similar case, see alış-veriş, ilanbalığı.
The term, which was previously attested as alğı-satqı, was later adapted to the colloquial language. The latest orthography dictionary does not include the original form.
Cognates
* Chuvash суту-илӳ (sut̬u-ilü, “commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Karachay-Balkar сатыу-алыу (satıu-alıu, “commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Kumyk сатыв-алыв (satıw-alıw, “commerce, trade”, literally “buying and buying”),
* Nogai сатув-алув (satuv-aluv, “commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Tatar сату-алу (satu-alu, “commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Turkish alım satım (“buying and selling”, literally “buying and selling”),
* Uyghur ئالدىـساتتى (aldi-satti, “commerce, trade”, literally “buying and selling”),
Compare
* Albanian shitblerje (“commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Burmese အရောင်းအဝယ် (a.raung:a.wai, “commerce, trade”, literally “selling and buying”),
* Central Kurdish كڕين و فرۆشتن (“commerce, trade”, literally “buying and selling”),
* Russian купля-продажа (kuplja-prodaža, “an instance of buying and selling”, literally “buying and selling”)
word_senses: purchase and sale as qualified in the Civil Code

head: dodaqlanmayan
etymology: From dodaqlan- (“to be pronounced by means of the lips”) + -ma (“negative verbal suffix”) + -yan (“subject non-past participle suffix”). Calque of Russian неогублённые (neogubljónnyje).
expansion: dodaqlan- (“to be pronounced by means of the lips”) + -ma (“negative verbal suffix”) + -yan (“subject non-past participle suffix”)

head: çalın
word_senses: cutting grass for hay; mowing, cutting the hay

head: durultmaq
word_senses: to thin, to make "less thick" (of blood, phlegm)

head: babadanqalma
etymology: From babadan + qalma. Literally, “inherited from grandfather”.
